memory_update.text: FORM should be tracked as a direct HBM probe-card/test-intensity beneficiary; key survival tests are HBM probe-card revenue growth, capacity expansion, and customer breadth.
ONTO is not small-cap but has unusually direct HBM4 process-control evidence via Dragonfly G5 selection by a leading HBM manufacturer.
KLIC remains an underfollowed advanced-packaging bonding candidate; verify whether thermocompression bonding is material enough to change the company’s legacy wire-bonder profile.
COHU is a lower-attention HBM inspection/test-handler hypothesis; the key evidence gap is materiality of HBM inspection versus broader cyclical test exposure.

Need a later pass for materials and consumables such as underfill, thermal interface materials, substrates, glass carriers, and specialty chemicals; this pass emphasized US-listed direct equipment and process-control companies.

summary: Expanded the HBM/advanced-packaging second-layer supplier universe toward US-listed direct equipment, inspection, probe/test, and bonding suppliers. The most relevant underfollowed lane candidates are FormFactor, Kulicke & Soffa, and Cohu; Onto Innovation is included as a higher-attention reference/direct supplier because its HBM4 inspection and metrology exposure appears unusually direct. This is a research universe only, not a buy/sell list.
